LZA Universal Configuration v.1.4.0 Desc: Shared VPC Model: Deploys a dedicated VPC with established  connectivity for each corresponding workload account (Dev, Test, Prod)

Note: This is an optional configuration that customers can choose to change. While the Hub-and-Spoke VPC Model is recommended, this architecture design may be appropriate for organizations where cost is a primary factor or if the workload does not require a more segmented approach. Customers should consider their security requirements, workload functionality and other related criteria when choosing the appropriate model for their organization.

LZA Universal Configuration v.1.4.0 Desc: Hub-and-Spoke VPC Model: Deploys resources across various VPCs designed to host different workloads, where data or resource access is governed by centralized "hub" infrastructure
Security & Compliance Implementation Det:
LZA Universal Configuration implements a Hub-and-Spoke VPC model, facilitating a regional architecture design that centralizes critical infrastructure components and supports information flow control between network segments.  The "hub" refers to centralized infrastructure (Transit Gateway, Direct Connect, Site-to-Site VPN, etc.) to which "spoke" VPCs leverage. Spoke VPCs are workload VPCs dependent on the hub for authorizing access to data or services.

The Hub-and-Spoke is the default VPC model in the LZA Universal Configuration. This approach helps facilitate logical separation of data flows and organizational information in distinct VPCs. The Hub-and-Spoke architecture baseline supports the implementation of boundary protection mechanisms, segmentation, and centralized access control.
